text: For the choirmaster. A psalm of David. LORD, you have searched me and you know me.
You know when I sit down and when I rise; you discern my thoughts from far away.
You mark my going out and my lying down; you are familiar with all my ways.
Not a word is on my tongue, LORD, but you know it completely.

versions.text: Before a word is on my tongue, LORD, you know it completely.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew says there is no word on the tongue that the LORD does not already know; "Before a word is on my tongue" adds a temporal idea not present in the text. The revised wording keeps the rhythm while staying closer to the Hebrew.

text: You hem me in, behind and before; you lay your hand upon me.
Such knowledge is too wonderful for me, too high for me to reach.
Where can I go from your Spirit? Where can I flee from your presence?
If I climb to the heavens, you are there; if I make my bed in Sheol, you are there.

versions.text: If I climb to the heavens, you are there; if I make my bed in the depths, you are there.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew names Sheol, the realm of the dead, which is a deliberate counterpart to "the heavens." "The depths" blurs this into a vague spatial image and loses the heaven/underworld contrast. A brief footnote explaining Sheol as the realm of the dead would help the hearer.

text: If I rise on the wings of the dawn and settle at the farthest edge of the sea,
even there your hand will guide me, your right hand will hold me fast.
If I say, "Surely the darkness will hide me, and the light around me turn to night,"
even the darkness is not dark to you; the night shines like the day, for darkness is as light to you.
For you created my inmost being; you knit me together in my mother's womb.
I praise you, for I am awesomely and wonderfully made. Your works are wonderful; my soul knows it well.
My frame was not hidden from you when I was made in secret, woven together in the depths of the earth.
Your eyes saw my unformed body; all my days were written in your book, ordained before a single one of them had come to be.

versions.text: Your eyes saw me before I was formed; all my days were written in your book, ordained before a single one of them had come to be.
versions.explanation: The noun golmi refers to the unformed substance or embryo itself, which God saw; the current wording shifts the meaning to a time reference ("before I was formed") and drops the concrete image.

text: How precious to me are your thoughts, O God! How vast is their number!
If I could count them, they would outnumber the grains of sand. When I awake, I am still with you.
If only you would slay the wicked, O God! Away from me, you men of blood!
They speak of you with malice; your enemies misuse your name.
Do I not hate those who hate you, LORD, and loathe those who rise against you?
I hate them with a perfect hatred; I count them my enemies.
Search me, O God, and know my heart; test me and know my anxious thoughts.
See if there is any offensive way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting.
